questions.stem: The Irani Trophy in Indian domestic cricket, played since 1959–60, is an annual contest between which two sides?

options.option_text: India A team versus the defending Duleep Trophy champions
The Ranji Trophy champions versus a Rest of India XI
The top two teams from the Ranji Trophy Super League stage
India Under-23 squad versus the current Ranji Trophy holders

questions.explanation: The Irani Trophy, instituted in 1959–60, is contested between the Ranji Trophy title-holders and a Rest of India XI selected by the BCCI. Option A is wrong because the Duleep Trophy is a separate zonal competition; confusing the two is the most frequent candidate error on this topic.

questions.stem: The Nehru Trophy Boat Race, famous for its traditional snake boats (Chundan Vallam), is held on which water body in Kerala?

options.option_text: Ashtamudi Lake near Kollam city in southern Kerala
Punnamada Lake near Alappuzha (Alleppey) in Kerala
Vellayani Lake near Thiruvananthapuram in Kerala
Paravur Lake near Ernakulam in central Kerala

questions.explanation: The Nehru Trophy Boat Race is held every second Saturday of August on Punnamada Lake, Alappuzha (Alleppey), Kerala. Option A (Ashtamudi Lake) is the most tempting distractor because it also hosts a famous boat race — the Champakkulam Moolam Boat Race — but that is a different event.

questions.stem: The Pataudi Trophy is awarded to the winner of the bilateral Test series between India and which country, and since which year was it so named?

options.option_text: Australia — series renamed after Pataudi's 1964 tour triumph
England — renamed the Pataudi Trophy after Tiger Pataudi in 2007
South Africa — instituted after India's historic 2006 series win
West Indies — named after Pataudi led India to a rare series victory

questions.explanation: The India–England Test series is contested for the Pataudi Trophy, named in 2007 in honour of Mansur Ali Khan Pataudi (Tiger Pataudi), the legendary Indian captain. Option A is wrong; India–Australia Tests are played for the Border-Gavaskar Trophy — conflating the two is the classic exam trap here.

questions.stem: The Rangaswami Cup, one of India's oldest sporting trophies instituted in 1928, is associated with which sport?

options.option_text: Lawn Tennis — named after the first Indian Davis Cup player
Football — a regional cup for south Indian state associations
Hockey — an inter-provincial tournament for club and state teams
Badminton — donated by a Mysore state official after Independence

questions.explanation: The Rangaswami Cup is a prestigious Indian hockey trophy instituted in 1928 and named after A. Rangaswami, former honorary secretary of the Indian Hockey Federation. Option B is the most tempting distractor because South India has many prominent football cups, but the Rangaswami Cup is unambiguously a hockey competition.

questions.stem: The Deodhar Trophy, a domestic One-Day cricket competition in India, is named in honour of which cricket personality?

options.option_text: D.B. Deodhar, a veteran Ranji-era cricketer and BCCI selector
Vasant Deodhar, the first BCCI secretary after Independence
P.R. Deodhar, a long-serving Maharashtra cricket board chairman
S.K. Deodhar, an Indian Olympian cricketer from the pre-war era

questions.explanation: The Deodhar Trophy honours Professor D.B. Deodhar (Datta Balkrishna Deodhar), a legendary pre-independence Indian batsman who later served as a BCCI selector and cricket administrator. Options B, C, and D use plausible but fictitious names to test whether candidates know the specific person being honoured.

questions.stem: The Ryder Cup in golf was originally contested between the USA and Great Britain. In 1979, the opposing side was broadened significantly. Who now opposes the USA in the Ryder Cup?

options.option_text: The Commonwealth of Nations, including Australia and South Africa
The Rest of the World, excluding the host nation's team entirely
Europe, encompassing Great Britain, Ireland, and continental Europe
Great Britain and Ireland only, unchanged from the original format

questions.explanation: From 1979, the opposing team in the Ryder Cup was expanded from Great Britain to a full European team (including continental European players such as Seve Ballesteros) to make the contest more competitive. Option D describes the pre-1979 format. Option A (Commonwealth) is a frequent misconception; Australia and South Africa do not participate in the Ryder Cup.

questions.stem: The Corbillon Cup is awarded at the World Table Tennis Championships as the direct counterpart of the Swaythling Cup. For which specific team event is the Corbillon Cup presented?

options.option_text: Mixed doubles team event at the world championships
Women's team event at the world championships
Under-21 junior boys team event at the championships
Para-athletes integrated team event at the championships

questions.explanation: The Corbillon Cup, donated by Marcel Corbillon (former French Table Tennis Federation official), is awarded to the winner of the women's team event at the World Table Tennis Championships — the direct female counterpart to the Swaythling Cup (men's teams). Option A is wrong; mixed doubles is an individual paired event, not a national team competition.
